argument_summary: Certification is supportable only on a caveated basis. The admissible record shows aggregate launch readiness passed by 2.2 percentage points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a 4% staged rollout with monitoring and rollback. The same record also shows a named weak exposed segment: the enterprise refund workflow remains below target on refund-policy summarization and is still included in the initial cohort. Because the risk-acceptance draft is incomplete and does not cover that exposure, the defensible position is not that rollout controls eliminate the issue, but that certification can proceed if the model card expressly discloses the enterprise refund workflow limitation at launch.
claims_about_business_cost: Business-cost considerations are not needed to justify the position. The narrow request is to avoid unnecessary escalation because the admissible record supports certification with a bounded compliance caveat rather than a broader noncompliance finding.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy does not allow rollout controls alone to cure this weakness when the affected use case remains exposed. It requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the limitation is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On the admissible evidence, approved risk acceptance is not established, so compliance depends on contemporaneous model-card disclosure of the known limitation. Aggregate readiness, monitoring, and rollback remain relevant as supplemental governance support, not as a substitute for disclosure.
concessions: The enterprise refund workflow segment is a real and currently exposed weakness.
The current risk-acceptance draft is not complete support because the approver line is blank and the draft does not address enterprise refund workflow exposure.
A small initial percentage, dashboard, and rollback switch do not by themselves remove the disclosure duty under the stated policy.
